problem_statement: This is the Ritz4U static commerce site (the RitanshRajput Ecommrece frontend template): a multi-page storefront with a Home page, a Shop listing, a single-product page, a Cart page, a Blog, an About page and a Contact page, all sharing one navbar (logo, Home / Shop / Blog / About / Contact links and a cart bag icon) and one footer. Product imagery is served from the local /products folder. The shop owner wants a small, consistent 'Fulfilment promise' rail that sits just above the footer on the shopping pages and reassures buyers about dispatch, delivery, returns and secure checkout - a labelled row of four tiles, each naming which local /products stock the promise ships from - plus a live cart badge next to the cart bag icon that updates when a shopper adds an item. Ship the Fulfilment promise rail so it (1) appears above the footer on the shopping pages - Home, Shop AND Cart, not just the Home page, (2) lays out its tile row responsively without horizontal overflow on a phone, (3) matches Ritz4U's own quiet light styling (white surface, light borders, dark text with the teal accent - not an off-palette dark slab), and (4) keeps the header cart badge in sync so that after a shopper clicks 'Add to cart' the badge reads the live count of one. Keep the rest of the site - the navbar, the footer, the product listings, the local /products assets - intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'Fulfilment promise' rail just above the footer on the shopping pages - Home, Shop AND Cart - with identical rail markup, not only the Home page.
The rail shows a 'Fulfilment promise' heading and a row of four tiles (Free dispatch, Two-day delivery, Easy returns, Secure checkout) each with a note naming the local /products stock it ships from.
The tile row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in Ritz4U's own quiet light language (white/near-white surface, light borders, dark text, teal accent), consistent and legible, not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the header cart badge next to the cart bag icon as a span with class `cart-count` and id `cartCount`, and mark the Home page 'Add to cart' control with a `data-add-to-cart` attribute: after clicking the `data-add-to-cart` button on the Home page, the badge (class `cart-count`, id `cartCount`) must read the live count '1' - it must re-read the live count, not rewrite a stale captured value.
Preserve the navbar, the footer, the product listings and the local /products assets with no console or network errors.
author_notes: Built on the RitanshRajput Ecommrece frontend template (the Ritz4U storefront), a static multi-page commerce site whose Home, Shop, single-product, Cart, Blog, About and Contact pages share one navbar and one footer and whose product art is served from the local /products stock folder. The Fulfilment promise rail is a shared markup block placed just above the footer on the shopping pages (Home, Shop, Cart); its four tiles each name the /products stock the promise ships from, grounding the rail in the site's own local asset story. The header cart badge reuses the existing cart bag icon as its anchor and is driven by a small shared assets/cart-badge.js Add-to-cart handler. The remote FontAwesome CDN link was revendored to a local FontAwesome stylesheet, and the remote freepik feature images and the Google Maps embed were replaced with local assets so the site runs offline with no network fetches. The responsive tile row, the light teal-accent design integration and the add-to-cart badge wiring were designed by hand for this Ritz4U storefront, not bulk-generated.
design_constraints: Implement the Fulfilment promise rail as one shared markup + stylesheet reused across the shopping pages so a single source of truth reaches Home, Shop and Cart; do not paste divergent copies or build a detached widget.
The tile row must use a fluid, wrapping responsive layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile; the tile spacing must stay legible.
The rail must adopt Ritz4U's own light surface/border/text language and teal accent so it reads as part of the storefront, not a foreign dark block.
The header cart badge must reflect the CURRENT cart count after every add-to-cart click by reading the live count, so it can never go stale relative to what the shopper added.
Do not remove or regress the navbar, the footer, the product listings or the local /products assets.

Expose the add-to-cart trigger with a `data-add-to-cart` attribute and render the header cart badge as a span with class `cart-count` (id `cartCount`) so the live-count wiring is testable: clicking the `data-add-to-cart` control must update the `cart-count` badge to the current count.

change_completion: The Fulfilment promise rail is present above the footer on Home, Shop AND Cart (the shared rail reaches all shopping pages, not just Home).
After clicking 'Add to cart' on the Home page, the header cart badge (cartCount) updates to '1' - the post-interaction terminal state changed from '0'.
design_consistency: The rail on the in-viewport states matches the reference's quiet light styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette dark slab.
The rail adopts Ritz4U's own white surface, light border, dark text and teal accent tokens so it reads as part of the storefront across the pages.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the tile row wraps.
mobile_initial, mobile_rail_home and tablet_rail_home keep the Fulfilment promise rail readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The navbar, the footer and the product listings remain present and functional across the pages.
The local /products assets and the static pages are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the Ritz4U home and responsive shell.
desktop_shop, mobile_shop and desktop_cart protect the existing shopping pages and carry the Fulfilment promise rail.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home scroll the Fulfilment promise rail into view and must show the light rail without horizontal overflow.
desktop_rail_shop and desktop_rail_cart protect the rail's presence on the Shop and Cart pages.
tablet_rail_home protects the rail's tablet layout without overflow.
add_to_cart_home clicks the Add-to-cart button; the header cart badge must then read '1'.
